perspectives.name: discovery-weak-signals

factors.name: revenueDiversification
factors.basis: Serve reported Q2 2026 revenue of $3.2 million, up 404% year over year, with recurring revenue above 50% of total revenue and seven multiyear hospital contract extensions plus two new hospitals in 1H 2026.

risks: Absolute revenue remains small relative to the company's operating-expense base.
unknowns: Durability and unit economics of each revenue stream are not established by headline growth alone.

perspectives.name: expectations-execution

factors.name: guidanceReset
factors.basis: Serve cut FY2026 revenue guidance to $9-$10 million from approximately $26 million previously, citing lower-than-expected Uber Eats delivery volume and removal of projected second-half demand, while lowering non-GAAP operating-expense guidance to $140-$150 million.

risks: The large revenue-guidance reset demonstrates material demand/execution uncertainty despite fleet and partnership expansion.
contradictions: Strong reported year-over-year growth and DoorDash sequential growth coexist with a major full-year revenue-guidance reduction due to Uber Eats volume weakness.
unknowns: Whether diversified recurring healthcare/advertising/software revenue can offset delivery-volume shortfalls in subsequent quarters.

facts: Q2 revenue was $3.2 million, up 404% year over year and 9% sequentially.
Recurring revenue exceeded 50% of total revenue.
FY2026 revenue guidance was revised to $9-$10 million because of lower-than-expected Uber Eats delivery volume and removal of projected second-half demand.
FY2026 non-GAAP operating-expense guidance was reduced to $140-$150 million.
Cash and marketable securities were $240.4 million at June 30, 2026.

result: Current Q2 execution evidence exposes both diversification progress and a material guidance miss for Alpha underwriting.
